repo.description: owner/name on GitHub; when left out, read from the origin remote

oneOf.description: GitHub Issues: a Feature is an issue with sub-issues, its Tickets

project.description: The project that holds the Features

featureType.description: The work item type that plays the Feature, such as Feature, Epic or Product Backlog Item

ticketType.description: The work item type nightjar create makes each Ticket as, such as User Story, Product Backlog Item or Issue. Left out, nightjar create makes no Tickets.

oneOf.description: Azure DevOps Boards: a Feature is a work item of featureType, its child work items its Tickets

path.description: The module that builds the Tracker, as a path from the repo's root

options.description: Handed to the module as it is, for its own settings

oneOf.description: A Tracker of the repo's own, built by a module

tracker.description: Where the Features and Tickets live

repo.description: owner/name on GitHub; when left out, read from the origin remote

trustedChecks.description: The slugs of the GitHub Apps whose failed checks on the pull request reach the agent as feedback, besides GitHub Actions, whose checks always do. A check from any other app is left out.

oneOf.description: GitHub: the branch is pushed to origin and a draft pull request opened

project.description: The project that holds the repo

repo.description: The Git repo on Azure Repos, by name

oneOf.description: Azure Repos: the branch is pushed to the repo and a draft pull request opened, signed in as for Azure DevOps Boards

path.description: The module that builds the Code host, as a path from the repo's root

options.description: Handed to the module as it is, for its own settings

oneOf.description: A Code host of the repo's own, built by a module

codeHost.description: Where the branch is pushed and the draft pull request opened

check.description: The shell command that checks the work in the worktree, run after each Ticket; it fails with a non-zero exit

failingTest.description: A regular expression, tried on each line of the check output and of each red stage log, whose first group names a failing test. Left out, a line of the form "FAIL name" matches.

ignore.description: A regular expression for lines that say nothing about why the check is red, such as notes about slow tests; they are left out of the report

stages.description: How to find the red stages when the check is split into stages. Left out, the report names none.

red.description: A regular expression, tried on each line of the check output, whose first group names a red stage

log.description: Where a red stage leaves its whole log, relative to the worktree, with {stage} for its name; its failing tests join the report

gate.description: What the report on a red check holds, so that the fix rounds and the pull request name every failing test and not only the end of the output

allowedCommands.description: The commands the agent may run, as Claude Code Bash permission patterns without Bash( ), such as "make test" or "make lint *". Committing, pushing, switching branches, the network and gh stay denied.

rules.description: A text file, relative to the repo root, whose text is added to the agent prompt. Conventions normally live in CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md.

plugins.description: Plugin directories, relative to the repo root, that every session loads (claude --plugin-dir). A restricted session ignores the repo's own .claude/skills, so a skill a Workflow Step names as /skill must come from one: [".claude"] loads the skills committed in .claude/skills.

model.description: The default model of every session; a Ticket's **Model:** line overrides it and --model overrides both

effort.description: The default effort of every session; a Ticket's **Effort:** line overrides it and --effort overrides both

review.description: The read-only review of the whole diff, run before the draft pull request opens

enabled.description: false switches the review off; on by default

model.description: The review session's own model; else the default model

effort.description: The review session's own effort; else the default effort

signals.description: The name each Signal has on a Tracker: a label on GitHub, a tag on Azure DevOps. Leave out the ones you do not rename. needs-triage and wontfix are refused.

go.description: The Go: put on a Feature assigned to you to have it built. Give it the name of ready to use one mark for both

ready.description: A Ticket that is ready to be built

needsInfo.description: Nightjar needs an answer to go on

human.description: A person has to take it from here

workflows.description: Work a repo adds to the build loop, by name. A Feature picks one with a **Workflow:** line; Nightjar still keeps the branch, the commits, the Signals and the pull request.

prompt.description: Text added to the build Session's instructions for each Ticket of a Feature that picks the Workflow, such as how to build a bug fix. A Workflow with a prompt may have no Steps.

name.description: The name of the Step; its commit and the pull request body name it

prompt.description: What the agent is told to do, such as "/some-skill critique"; it may name any skill. Nightjar adds the rule that nobody is at the keyboard.

point.description: afterEachTicket runs after each Ticket is built; afterAllTickets runs once, after every Ticket, before the review

model.description: The Step's own model; else the default model

effort.description: The Step's own effort; else the default effort

budgetUsd.description: The most one run of the Step may cost in dollars; else a Ticket's budget

until.description: A condition in plain words. After each round the agent reports whether it holds, and Nightjar runs the Step again until it does or maxRounds is reached

maxRounds.description: The most rounds of a Step with an until; 3 when left out

serve.description: A command started in the background in the worktree before the Workflow's Steps and stopped after them, such as a dev server. It reads its port from the variables of ports.env, so it needs ports.

allowedCommands.description: Commands the Workflow's Steps may run besides the top-level allowedCommands, as Bash permission patterns without Bash( )

allowedTools.description: Tools the Workflow's Steps may use besides the usual ones, as Claude Code permission rules. Committing, pushing, switching branches, the outside network and gh stay denied.

localNetwork.description: true lets the Workflow's Steps reach localhost, and nothing else on the network

additionalProperties.description: A named list of Steps, and a prompt for each Ticket, that a Feature picks with a **Workflow:** line

sources.description: Where Features come from besides a person, by name. nightjar intake receives their webhooks and fires their schedules, and makes each Feature on the Tracker; it never builds.

type.description: schedule fires from a cron time, webhook takes a signed webhook of the Standard Webhooks scheme, sentry takes a Sentry alert

cron.description: When a schedule fires, in the machine's local time zone: five cron fields, @daily or @weekly. A schedule needs it; a webhook has none.

template.description: A Feature file as a path from the repo's root, or the name of a template Nightjar ships, such as sentry or weekly-deps

key.description: A path into the payload, such as data.event.issue_id, that says when two events are the same; while a Feature with the same key is open, no new one is made

secretEnv.description: The environment variable that holds the webhook secret; the secret is never in factory.json

maxPerDay.description: The most Features the Source makes in a day; 3 when left out

go.description: true gives each Feature the Go, assigned to the owner. Left out, the Go stays with a person. Needs an owner.

owner.description: The login a Feature with the Go is assigned to; the Tracker must trust them (on Azure DevOps, a sign-in name such as ann@contoso.com)

additionalProperties.description: Makes Features with nobody writing them: a schedule or a signed webhook, each from a template. nightjar intake runs it.

defaultWorkflow.description: The Workflow of a Feature without a **Workflow:** line; none when left out

trusted.description: The logins whose comments reach the agent (on Azure DevOps, sign-in names such as ann@contoso.com). When set, it replaces the Tracker default (GitHub: write access; Azure DevOps: the project's Contributors group); leave it out to keep the default.

setup.description: The shell command run once in each new worktree, before the first session, such as one that installs dependencies. When it fails, the Feature stops with a comment saying why. Left out, nothing is run.

ports.description: Ports reserved for each run and held for its whole life, so that two runs on one machine never share a port. Left out, no port is held.

env.description: The environment variables that carry the ports to every session, the check and the setup command: the first name gets the first reserved port, the next name the next port, and so on

pullChecks.description: The pass over Nightjar's own red draft pull requests: it fixes their failed Pull checks until a person engages with the pull request

enabled.description: true has Nightjar fix the failed Pull checks of its own draft pull requests before it takes the next Feature; off by default

fixRounds.description: How many Pull-check fix rounds one pull request may get, counted from its branch's commits; 2 when left out. After them, the Feature gets the needs-a-person Signal

fixUsd.description: The most one Pull-check fix round may cost in dollars, its check's fix rounds too; 5 when left out

fixMinutes.description: The most minutes one Pull-check fix round may run, its check's fix rounds too; 30 when left out
